Humanoids: coverage & development

Robot Body Atlas v0.2.1 · Snapshot: 29 October 2026. This is a research catalogue, not a standardized independent benchmark or a procurement ranking.

The interface, filters and catalogue summaries support Chinese and English. Source-specific technical notes, manufacturer documents, papers, JSON downloads and the original performance workbook retain their original language. Translation does not change a numeric value, unit, evidence level or hardware revision.

Coverage

The full Humanoid Intel reference index contains 43 models (source update: 22 September 2026). Version-specific expansion produces 56 records: 38 have at least one primary source, while 18 remain reference-only. Primary-source coverage does not mean every metric is complete. There are 198 primary-source numeric values with units, conditions and citations.

Coverage includes 14 Unitree configurations across G1, G1+, R1, H1/H1-2, H2, H2-X and H2 Plus; Chinese platforms from Booster, Fourier, AGIBOT, UBTECH, ENGINEAI, LimX, ROBOTERA, Astribot, Xiaomi and Galbot; and international platforms including Atlas, Digit, Apollo, NEO, Figure, 4NE1, AEON, HMND and Phoenix.

Reference values and primary evidence

The default view uses primary-source specifications only. Missing values display — and are excluded by active numeric filters. The optional reference view fills only missing fields with unverified reference values marked †. Cards, sorting, filters, comparison and CSV use the same selected scope. The Evidence & reference index tab preserves the original reference row alongside primary-source values.

Compare the same hardware scope

  • Whole-body DOF may include or exclude hands, wrists or the base. Read each condition.
  • Single-arm payload and robot/two-arm carrying payload are separate. A vague payload claim is kept in notes rather than assigned to an unsupported category.
  • Walking, running, wheeled-base and end-effector speeds are distinct. End-effector speed is not locomotion speed.
  • Standby, walking and task runtime retain their original test conditions and inequality bounds.

Version discrepancies

Atlas uses the explicitly identified 2026 commercial version. NEO Beta and current NEO are separate records. Digit v4, Apollo 1, 4NE1 V7 and Phoenix generation 6 retain their generations rather than borrowing current-generation specifications. H1 Pro has no confirmed official mapping and is not treated as H1-2. Galbot G1’s V2.0 manual reports 92.5 kg, distinct from the reference index’s 55 kg. Galbot DOF is a documented component sum excluding the base and end effector.

Next work

Complete primary evidence and images for the 18 reference-only records; review Optimus, Atom, Tiangong, PUDU D9, Walker X and Kepler; add new generations separately. Expand body/hand DOF, reach, joint architecture, transmission, sensors and interfaces. Map actuator and hand IDs only when explicit evidence identifies the hardware. Add papers, laboratory adoption and independent measurements.

Maintenance

Edit research/humanoids/primary-*.json, then run scripts/build-humanoids.py. Each metric needs a value, unit, source and condition; inequalities use qual. Preserve stable IDs, exact baselineNames and original snapshots. See the full Chinese handoff for the pending-model list and data schema.

Read the full original Chinese handoff for the complete source-language technical record. The English page is a maintained guide, not a replacement for the original evidence.
